title: One hand; sanctified Son; Lazarus illness (John 10:27–11:4)
english: Proof of the Lord's sheep is readiness to hear; of strangers, disobedience. For hearing here means obeying what is said, and following means imitation through deeds. He says he gives life, which he also calls eternal: living in cheer and unbroken blessedness. And to perish into the age means to be subject to unceasing torments. By his hand he means the power and authority from which no one can snatch those who follow him. And even if as God by nature he himself gives from himself, yet as man he is also said to receive. He says this not as if through the Father's power alone no one snatches them because he himself is insufficient to keep them, but so they may not call him opposed to God; for he said beforehand that no one snatches them from my hand, and showing that this hand is one, he says it is sometimes his and sometimes the Father's; for he himself is the Father's right hand. Then lest through these words someone think the Son less than the Father, he added next: "I and the Father are one" (John 10:30)—clearly according to the power which he also calls hand.

Signifying that Father and Son are not one according to hypostasis, he said "I and the Father"; for they are one in essence, in the power which he also calls hand, sometimes his and sometimes the Father's.

The works are not mine alone but of the whole Godhead; for the Father does all things through the Son in the Holy Spirit, and he teaches us to be moderate and not boast if we receive something from God.
Not knowing that the Son was not going to sojourn with bare Godhead but incarnate "from David's seed" (Romans 1:3), they called the right confession blasphemy.
If Israelites, filthy humans who received this by grace, are not charged, how is the one who has this by nature rebuked?
The Son is said to be sanctified because he was sent to be slaughtered for the world's salvation; for holy are the things set apart to God for sacrifice.
Since seeing the essence is impossible, from equality of works he presents the indistinguishability of power, through which he says the Father is known from himself and he himself from the Father.

"I am in the Father and the Father is seen in me" according to identity of nature and essence; for one is the definition of nature, even if we conceive the holy Trinity in distinct existences; for the Father is not Son or Spirit nor the reverse, even if they are not in separation because of their mutual communion and equality; for even among us the begetter's essence is known and in the begotten the father according to the account of essence, yet because we are separated by bodies, we the many are no longer "one."
From how easily he escapes them even against their will, it is shown that he would not have been caught unless willing.

He came there to remind the crowds of what John said about him. Those who cross the mystical Jordan are carried toward God, just as Christ, having crossed the Jordan, came into the church of the nations and remained there.
This is not the woman Matthew and Luke mention; for those were prostitutes, whom Christ endured through goodness.
She did this to wipe a blessing from the holy flesh.
